# Pre-Plan Readiness Checklist: HumanWorkUnit and Safe Resume v1

**Purpose**: Validate the QUALITY and COMPLETENESS of the requirements themselves — not the implementation — before `/speckit-plan` is run
**Created**: 2026-08-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Audience**: Maintainer / reviewer, at the pre-plan gate
**Rigor**: Standard-to-deep

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**How to read an item**: every line asks whether something is *written well enough* in `spec.md` — complete, unambiguous, consistent, measurable, covered. No line asks whether code behaves correctly. An item that cannot be answered from the spec alone is itself the finding.

---

## Cluster 1 — Authorization, One-Task Binding, Isolation and Minimum Projection

- [x] CHK001 Are the worker-side recheck obligations enumerated completely — approved status, category, tier, prior-delivery rules, unit-to-task binding, active claim holder, claim generation, classification projection — with none left to inference? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK002 Is the absence of worker-side tenant membership stated as a positive, checkable requirement rather than only as an omission, so a later reintroduction would be detectable? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK003 Are client-side and admin-side access requirements stated separately from worker-side requirements, each naming its own gating rule? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, §Authorization and Data Classification]
- [x] CHK004 Is cross-client isolation defined as an enforceable structural property — one unit bound to one task and one accepted contract, plus minimum-necessary projection — rather than as an outcome to be achieved by unspecified means? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements defined for the case where a declared input's classification is broader than the unit's permitted reach, naming whether publication is withheld or the run fails closed? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK006 Does the spec define the forbidden-in-worker-projection field set in a way that stays correct as new fields are added, rather than as a fixed enumeration that silently stops protecting? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014, §FR-054]
- [x] CHK007 Is "minimum necessary inputs" defined with criteria a reviewer can apply to a concrete plan, or does it rest entirely on the plan author's judgment? [Measurability, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-014]
- [x] CHK008 Are requirements specified for whether a worker retains visibility of the unit's inputs after submission, after a rejection, and after the run has resumed? [Gap, Spec §FR-014, §User Story 4]
- [x] CHK009 Are the consequences of a mid-run change to platform eligibility configuration specified for a worker already holding the task, distinctly from an individual approval being withdrawn? [Gap, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-043]
- [x] CHK010 Is it specified whether the accepted human result and its artifacts inherit the mandate's data classification for downstream steps, evidence retention and admin surfaces? [Gap, Spec §FR-040, §FR-041]

## Cluster 2 — Fixed Payout, One Claimant, No Second Engagement, No Inferred Economics

- [x] CHK011 Is the figure shown to a worker before claiming identified unambiguously as the accepted fixed task payout, and distinguished from the residual figure used on the unadmitted path? [Clarity, Spec §FR-034, §Economics]
- [x] CHK012 Does the prohibition on moving that payout explicitly cover the later completion handover, and not only the moment of claim? [Completeness, Spec §FR-034]
- [x] CHK013 Are requirements defined for how the admitted path interacts with the existing residual payout computation — bypassed, constrained, or applied with a stated invariant? [Gap, Spec §FR-034, §FR-036]
- [x] CHK014 Is "exactly one payable worker per task" stated as a requirement with a defined refusal behaviour when a second claimant is attempted, rather than as a design intention? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, §FR-033]
- [x] CHK015 Are "second engagement", "per-unit payout" and "partial payout" defined precisely enough that a reviewer could recognise a violation in a proposed design? [Clarity, Spec §FR-033]
- [x] CHK016 Is "zero provider spend while waiting" bounded by a definition of what counts as provider spend, so that neither non-provider cost is smuggled in nor a false zero is claimed? [Clarity, Spec §FR-031, §SC-006]
- [x] CHK017 Are the states across which the zero-spend guarantee must hold enumerated — waiting, claimed, submitted, in review, revision requested — rather than stated only for the two endpoints? [Completeness, Spec §FR-031]
- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for the frozen automation budget ceiling when a run pauses for an admin and later continues, including that the pause cannot re-derive it? [Gap, Spec §FR-032, §FR-037]
- [x] CHK019 Does the prohibition on inferring economics cover derivation, splitting and apportionment, not only outright invention of a new figure? [Completeness, Spec §FR-035]
- [x] CHK020 Is the criterion for "effort cannot honestly be shown to sit within the accepted reserved effort and payout" expressed so that two reviewers would reach the same admission verdict on the same plan? [Measurability, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-035, §User Story 3]

## Cluster 3 — Concurrency, Leases and Generations, Duplicate Acceptance and Resume, Crash Recovery, Cancellation, Deadlines, Fail-Closed Ownership

- [x] CHK021 Are the claim generation and the resume generation defined as distinct concepts, each with its scope of monotonicity and its own refusal rule? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, §FR-027]
- [x] CHK022 Is the atomicity binding a unit claim to the task's sole worker assignment stated as one indivisible outcome, including what must hold if either half cannot complete? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK023 Are exactly-once requirements stated per trigger class — concurrent triggers, retries, scheduled sweeps, crashes, replays — rather than as one undifferentiated claim? [Completeness, Spec §FR-026, §SC-005]
- [x] CHK024 Are recovery requirements defined for a crash between submission and candidate persistence, separately from a crash between acceptance and resume? [Gap, Spec §FR-029]
- [x] CHK025 Is the set of lifecycle states that must refuse a resume enumerated exhaustively, with no open-ended "or similar" wording? [Completeness, Spec §FR-028]
- [x] CHK026 Are duplicate-action refusals specified separately for a duplicate submission and a duplicate review decision, each naming which record survives and what the losing actor is told? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018, §FR-020]
- [x] CHK027 Are deadline values, their starting events and their expiry consequences stated in requirements, or do they exist only as assumptions that no requirement enforces? [Traceability, Gap, Spec §FR-044, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK028 Is a notification or alerting obligation specified for a deadline lapse or an admin pause, or is aggregate queryability the only visibility the requirements promise? [Gap, Spec §FR-044, §Observability]
- [x] CHK029 Are requirements defined for whether a submitted candidate is retained as evidence when the mandate is cancelled or the unit is withdrawn, as distinct from when it is rejected? [Gap, Spec §FR-041, §FR-042]
- [x] CHK030 Is "still eligible" in the post-resume failure routing rule defined against the same eligibility set used at claim time, rather than left as a separate undefined judgment? [Clarity, Spec §FR-045, §FR-009]
- [x] CHK031 Are requirements specified for downstream failure when the original claimant is no longer eligible, naming who owns the pause and what the worker is told? [Coverage, Spec §FR-045]
- [x] CHK032 Can the requirement that no fail-closed path leaves a run without an owner and a next action be checked row by row against the exception table? [Measurability, Spec §FR-046, §Failure Modes and Exception States]
- [x] CHK033 Does the admission rule define its behaviour for a dependency cycle or a dependency on a step that does not exist, or does it assume a well-formed graph? [Gap, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK034 Are "ancestor" and "descendant" defined against the accepted plan's dependency graph, so the one-cut topology test is applied identically by every reader? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, §Assumptions]

## Cluster 4 — State Visibility, Gate Separation, Rollout and Rollback

- [x] CHK035 Are the admin-visible attributes of a waiting run enumerated — cause, authorized actor, deadline, revisions remaining, next action — and each defined well enough to be rendered without further interpretation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-052]
- [x] CHK036 Are worker-facing visibility requirements specified for the period after acceptance, while the worker still holds the task and machine steps are running? [Gap, Spec §FR-052, §User Story 4]
- [x] CHK037 Are client-facing visibility requirements specified for a mandate waiting mid-run, or is client-side behaviour explicitly declared unchanged? [Gap, Spec §Out of Scope]
- [x] CHK038 Is the separation between submission, internal admin acceptance, final quality review and delivery stated as four gates with distinct preconditions, rather than as narrative? [Completeness, Spec §Verification and Delivery Conditions]
- [x] CHK039 Are requirements defined for a final quality review rejecting a delivery whose human unit was already accepted, including whether that acceptance can be reopened? [Gap, Spec §Verification and Delivery Conditions, §FR-023]
- [x] CHK040 Is "schema conformance is a precondition for submission and never evidence of correctness" expressed in requirement form, not only as commentary? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, §Verification and Delivery Conditions]
- [x] CHK041 Are rollout and rollback obligations expressed as testable requirements or success criteria, rather than existing only as a prose section with no FR or SC behind them? [Traceability, Gap, Spec §Rollout and Rollback]
- [x] CHK042 Is the behaviour of runs already waiting on a human unit specified for the moment the rollout control is disabled? [Coverage, Spec §Rollout and Rollback]
- [x] CHK043 Is it required that no historical run, package, payout or audit record changes meaning as a result of this feature or of its rollback? [Completeness, Spec §Rollout and Rollback, §FR-039]
- [x] CHK044 Is an append-only or tamper-evidence obligation stated for the human-unit audit trail, consistent with the platform's existing audit rules? [Gap, Spec §FR-048, §FR-050]

## Scenario Coverage — Primary and Alternate Flows

- [x] CHK045 Does every transition of the primary flow — pre-human block, publication, claim, submission, acceptance, resume, completion — own at least one requirement, with no transition described only in a user story? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1]
- [x] CHK046 Are alternate-flow requirements defined for a rejection followed by a successful revision within the bound? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 2, §FR-021]
- [x] CHK047 Are alternate-flow requirements defined for a voluntary release before submission, naming the effect on the revision counter and on the run's waiting state? [Coverage, Spec §FR-015, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK048 Are requirements defined for a voluntary release *after* a revision was requested, including whether the remaining revision count carries to the next claimant? [Gap, Spec §FR-015, §FR-022]
- [x] CHK049 Are requirements defined for a revision remaining available while no eligible worker re-claims the unit before the deadline? [Gap, Spec §FR-044, §FR-021]
- [x] CHK050 Are requirements defined for a partial resume, where some downstream steps are ineligible for a non-human reason and the run continues with the remainder? [Coverage, Spec §FR-025, §User Story 1]

## Scenario Coverage — Exception and Recovery Flows

- [x] CHK051 Does every row of the exception table name a trigger, a resolution owner and a guaranteed outcome, with no row resolving to "existing behaviour" without saying what that behaviour guarantees? [Completeness, Spec §Failure Modes and Exception States]
- [x] CHK052 Are exception requirements defined for a claim attempted against a task that already has a different claimant, distinctly from an ordinary contention loss? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011, §User Story 4]
- [x] CHK053 Are recovery requirements defined for a stale holder submitting after reassignment, naming refusal rather than merge or overwrite? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK054 Are requirements defined for two admins deciding simultaneously, naming which decision survives and what the loser is shown? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK055 Is it required that unsupported-topology and unmapped-economics refusals be reported in their own terms, never as a missing capability and never as a budget demotion? [Consistency, Spec §FR-038, §FR-053]

## Requirement Consistency, Conflicts and Ambiguities

- [x] CHK056 Do the frozen "expected minutes" field and the prohibition on inferring economics from unit duration conflict, given that expected minutes also seeds the default claim lease? [Conflict, Spec §FR-002, §FR-035, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK057 Is terminology for the acting roles consistent — "VA", "worker", "approved worker", "claimant", "admin" — or do synonyms appear without a stated equivalence? [Consistency, Spec §Clarifications, §FR-009]
- [x] CHK058 Are the unit's revision bound and the customer-facing revision rounds distinguished everywhere both appear, so neither can be read as the other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK059 Do the payout-immutability requirement and the existing rule refusing unproven payout reductions agree, without one implying a recomputation the other forbids? [Consistency, Spec §FR-034, §FR-036]
- [x] CHK060 Are the fail-closed outcomes described identically across the user stories, the functional requirements and the exception table? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 3, §FR-046, §Failure Modes and Exception States]

## Dependencies, Assumptions and Constitution Obligations

- [x] CHK061 Is each assumption marked as a revisable informed default, and has any assumption carrying a safety property been promoted to a requirement instead? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK062 Are the reused platform mechanisms enumerated as explicit dependencies, so a future change to any of them is known to affect this feature? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK063 Does every factual claim about existing behaviour carry an evidence label, and do aggregate claims carry the weakest label among their inputs? [Traceability, Spec §Evidence Labels]
- [x] CHK064 Are the deferred commercial `UNKNOWN`s stated with their denominator, so a later reader can see the feature was selected against unmeasured demand? [Traceability, Spec §Problem Statement and Evidence]
- [x] CHK065 Does the constitution compliance section name the principles this change puts at risk, and does a specific requirement address each named risk? [Traceability, Spec §Constitution Compliance Check]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality and Traceability

- [x] CHK066 Is every success criterion measurable without knowledge of the implementation, including the 30-second admin comprehension criterion? [Measurability, Spec §SC-010]
- [x] CHK067 Does each of the four review clusters have at least one success criterion that would fail if that cluster's requirements were violated? [Coverage, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [x] CHK068 Are the zero-valued success criteria stated with the population they are measured over, rather than as unqualified zeroes? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003, §SC-005, §SC-006]
- [x] CHK069 Is every functional requirement traceable to at least one user story, edge case or success criterion, with no orphan requirement? [Traceability, Spec §Requirements]
- [x] CHK070 Is the requirement identifier scheme stable enough for the plan and tasks to reference without renumbering churn, given the FR/SC renumbering already performed during clarification? [Traceability, Spec §Requirements]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`; this file is reviewer-owned and is not maintained by those commands
- Add comments or findings inline beneath the item they concern
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
- Items carrying a `[Gap]` marker are the ones most likely to require a spec edit before `/speckit-plan`; they are concentrated in CHK008–CHK010, CHK013, CHK018, CHK024, CHK027–CHK029, CHK033, CHK036–CHK037, CHK039, CHK041, CHK044, CHK048–CHK049
